title: Late-night homicide solved on call-tower + deleted SMS
description: Accused Ramesh was suspected in the murder of deceased Sunil after a property dispute. Deceased was last seen leaving his shop at 22:10. Accused denied being at the scene.

artifacts.note: Two calls to the deceased at 22:04 and 22:31 contradicted the accused's alibi.
Cell-tower and GPS placed the handset within 400 m of the scene at 22:20.
Deleted SMS recovered from SQLite freelist contained a threat sent three days earlier.
Established the accused-deceased relationship.
Bulk gallery pull produced nothing of evidentiary value; 40 minutes of acquisition wasted.
No relevant history.

lessons: In homicide, movement + call graph around the time of death carry the case.
Bulk media is usually dead weight unless scene or weapon photographs are alleged.

title: Homicide where gallery media was the decisive artifact
description: Accused Faisal was suspected of killing deceased Anwar. Accused claimed the weapon was never in his possession.

artifacts.note: A trashed photograph with intact EXIF GPS showed the accused holding the weapon two days before the offence.
The image had been moved to .trashed- and was recovered from shared storage.
EXIF GPS on the photo corroborated the recovery site.
Contact with a co-accused on the day of the offence.
Device unrooted; msgstore.db encrypted and unreadable.

lessons: Media is not always low value in homicide — when a weapon or scene photograph is alleged, it becomes the case.
Trashed-media recovery outperformed live gallery listing.

title: Narcotics supply chain mapped from chat + payment traces
description: Accused Imran and co-accused Salim were suspected of supplying contraband. Complainant was an NCB source. Consignment drops were coordinated over messaging apps.

artifacts.note: Root-recovered cache4.db held drop coordinates and quantities.
UPI SMS alerts matched consignment dates and amounts.
Buyer/supplier graph identified nine downstream peddlers.
GPS clusters at three repeat drop points.
Bank alerts and delivery confirmations.
Empty.
No probative value.

lessons: Narcotics cases live in encrypted chat plus payment traces, not voice calls.
Repeat GPS clusters identify drop points faster than reading every message.

title: Peddling case carried by call-log pattern alone
description: Suspect Gopal was detained with a small quantity. No chat applications were installed on the handset.

artifacts.note: Forty-one short calls to eleven numbers in one week — classic street-level distribution pattern.
Repeat callers resolved to known consumers.
Two coded delivery messages.
App not installed; Tier-2 pull attempted and wasted.
App not installed.
Personal photos only.

lessons: Check the installed-app inventory before spending Tier-2 effort on chat databases.
Call-frequency shape can substitute for message content in street-level supply.

title: Investment fraud proven from SMS bank alerts and browser history
description: Complainant Meera reported that accused Vivek induced her to transfer funds to a fake investment scheme.

artifacts.note: Transaction SMS chain traced funds through three mule accounts.
OTP and transfer alerts established the timeline.
History showed the spoofed brokerage domain and its registration page.
Multiple payment-app accounts under different identities on one device.
Solicitation messages present in an exported chat text file.
Irrelevant to the offence.
Screenshots of fake returns had no independent value.

lessons: Fraud is a paper trail: SMS alerts plus browser artifacts usually outrank chat content.
Location data is near-useless in pure financial fraud — deprioritise it.

title: Loan-app extortion traced through installed apps and accounts
description: Complainant Arjun reported coercive recovery calls after using a predatory lending application. Suspects unknown at intake.

artifacts.note: Installed loan applications with excessive contact/SMS permissions identified the operator.
Device accounts linked the operator's identity.
Harassment call pattern from VOIP ranges.
Threat messages.
Recovered removed application records.
Nothing relevant.

lessons: The installed-app inventory is a first-class artifact in app-mediated fraud, not a low-priority extra.
Dangerous-permission grants point straight at the offending application.

title: Kidnapping resolved on ransom-call trail and movement history
description: Victim Ananya was abducted. Complainant, her father, received ransom demands. Accused Bilal was identified after handset analysis.

artifacts.note: Ransom call sequence and duration pattern.
Movement history led to the confinement site and a live recovery.
Co-accused identification.
Drop-point instructions.
Encrypted; unrooted device.
No relevant history.
No relevant media.

lessons: Kidnapping is time-critical: location history first, everything else second.
Prioritise artifacts that can be acted on within hours over deep recovery.

title: POCSO case established on private-chat media and deleted images
description: Accused Naveen was reported by complainant for sending obscene material to the victim, a minor. Device seized under warrant.

artifacts.note: Gallery and thumbnail cache held the offending images; hash-matched to the complaint.
Deleted image records recovered from the media store freelist.
Root-recovered direct.db held the sending thread.
Arroyo database showed contact but no retained content.
Established prior acquaintance.
No calls between the parties.
Not applicable.

lessons: Media and private-chat applications are the case in sexual-offence matters — never deprioritise them.
Thumbnail caches survive deletion of the original and are worth carving.

title: Sextortion network traced via browser, accounts and crypto traces
description: Complainant Rohit reported extortion following a video call. Suspects operated from outside the jurisdiction.

artifacts.note: History and cache exposed the payment portal and the hosting panel.
Throwaway accounts linked five victim reports to one operator.
Crypto wallet addresses recovered from clipboard and messages.
Channel membership showed the distribution group.
Sideloaded application used for the calls.
All contact was over IP; carrier call log empty.
No probative value.

lessons: In cybercrime the carrier call log is usually empty — do not weight it high.
Browser and account artifacts outrank message content for attribution.

title: Data-theft insider identified from app usage and cloud accounts
description: Complainant company reported exfiltration of customer records. Suspect Deepak was an employee with device access.

artifacts.note: App-usage statistics showed a file-sync client in the foreground at the exfiltration window.
A personal cloud account was added two days before the incident.
Install timestamp of the sync client.
Access to the internal portal outside working hours.
Removed application traces recovered.
No relevant media.
No relevant messages.

lessons: App-usage statistics are frequently dismissed as low value but are decisive for insider timing questions.
Account addition events are a strong exfiltration signal.

title: Stalking and threat case built entirely from messaging threads
description: Complainant Pooja reported persistent threats from accused Karan across multiple platforms after she ended contact.

artifacts.note: Exported chat text file in shared storage preserved the threat sequence.
Direct-message thread continued after the block.
Two hundred and eleven call attempts in nine days established persistence.
Threats from an alternate number.
Recovered messages the accused had removed.
Repeated presence near the complainant's residence.
No relevant media.
Not applicable.

lessons: Call-attempt frequency is itself evidence of persistence, independent of content.
Exported WhatsApp .txt files in Download often survive when the database cannot be read.

title: Vehicle theft ring exposed by location clustering and resale chatter
description: Accused Sameer was suspected in a series of two-wheeler thefts. Complainants filed across four police stations.

artifacts.note: GPS clusters matched four theft sites and one common dismantling yard.
Co-accused contact immediately after each theft window.
Resale negotiation in an exported chat.
Photographs of stolen vehicles sent to buyers.
Buyer identification.
Nothing relevant.
Empty.

lessons: Repeat GPS clustering across separate complaints links cases that were filed independently.
Movement analysis outperformed message reading for establishing the pattern.

title: Missing person located from last-known movement and travel search
description: Complainant reported that Neha, aged nineteen, left the residence and was untraceable. No offence alleged at intake.

artifacts.note: Last GPS fix at a bus terminal narrowed the search radius immediately.
Ticket-booking searches identified the destination city.
Final outgoing call to a friend.
Recent contact with a person in the destination city.
Identified that contact.
Deep recovery ran for fifty minutes and produced nothing; time-critical case.
No probative value.

lessons: Missing-person work is a search problem, not a forensic-recovery problem — deep carving wastes the critical window.
Browser search history is often the single fastest lead.

title: Conspiracy case requiring all-source collection
description: Accused Yusuf and co-accused were suspected of planning an attack. Handset seized during a coordinated operation.

artifacts.note: Channel content and handler contact recovered from cache4.db.
Repeat visits to the target site established reconnaissance.
Reconnaissance photographs with EXIF GPS on the target premises.
Searches for materials and site layout.
Funding transfers.
Wiped chat fragments carved from freelist pages.
Cell membership.
No probative value.

lessons: Conspiracy cases are the exception where nothing should be deprioritised — collect all sources.
Reconnaissance is visible as repeat location visits plus geotagged media of the same place.

title: Homicide where the notification log preserved deleted message content
description: Accused Prakash was suspected in the death of deceased Manoj. The accused wiped the messaging application before seizure.

artifacts.note: Notification-history records preserved message previews after the application data was cleared.
Contact pattern consistent with the preserved previews.
Placed the handset on the route to the scene.
Application data-clear timestamp evidenced destruction of evidence.
Database wiped; nothing recoverable even with root.
Nothing relevant.

outcome: Charge-sheeted with an added destruction-of-evidence count.
lessons: When a chat application has been wiped, the system notification log is the highest-value remaining source.
Application data-clear timestamps are themselves evidence.

title: Blackmail case resolved from Wi-Fi and Bluetooth association history
description: Complainant Ishita reported blackmail by an unknown person who demonstrated physical proximity. Suspect Ajay was identified later.

artifacts.note: Wi-Fi association history placed the suspect handset on the complainant's residential network.
Paired-device names resolved to the suspect.
Demand messages from a burner number.
The material used for the blackmail was present in a hidden directory.
No direct calls.

lessons: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth association history is proximity evidence and belongs alongside GPS, not below it.
Burner-number cases still leave device-association traces.

title: Cheating case where screen-time and usage statistics disproved a defence
description: Accused Nilesh claimed the handset was not in his possession during the disputed transfers. Complainant Ravi disputed this.

artifacts.note: Continuous foreground activity across the disputed window disproved the not-in-possession defence.
Payment application transaction records.
Bank alerts.
Single account throughout.
Handset never left the accused's residence.
Not relevant.
Not installed.

lessons: Usage and screen-time statistics answer possession and presence questions that no message can.
Always collect the cheap behavioural artifacts — they defeat alibi defences.

title: Custodial abduction where calendar and travel artifacts carried the case
description: Complainant Sneha reported that accused Manish removed their child from lawful custody and left the state.

artifacts.note: A travel entry created before the removal established premeditation.
Ticket and accommodation searches identified the destination.
Route reconstruction supported interception.
Booking confirmations tied to a specific account.
Contact with a relative at the destination.
Nothing additional recovered.

lessons: Calendar entries are routinely deprioritised but prove premeditation in planned-removal cases.
Travel-intent artifacts (calendar, browser, accounts) cluster together and should be planned as a group.
